\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{خلع} (khalaʿa)}{خلع (khalaʿa)}]{\ar{خلع} (khalaʿa) — to take off (clothes)}

\label{lesson:AR-C193-khalaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to receive, then the Arabic for to cost.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{خلع}}
\textbf{\ar{خلع}} — \emph{khalaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to take off (clothes)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{خلع}} (\emph{khalaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-l-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to pull off\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Khalaʿa} is the plain verb, \textquotedblleft{}he took off\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khalaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{khalaʿa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to receive, then the Arabic for to cost, then say \emph{khalaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\end{cousinweb}
